## **Problem**

Given two [strings](https://rosalind.info/glossary/string/) ss and tt of equal length, the [**Hamming distance**](https://rosalind.info/glossary/hamming-distance/) between ss and tt, denoted dH(s,t)dH(s,t), is the number of corresponding symbols that differ in ss and tt. See [**Figure 2**](https://rosalind.info/media/problems/hamm/Hamming_distance.png).

**Given:** Two [DNA strings](https://rosalind.info/glossary/dna-string/) ss and tt of equal length (not exceeding 1 [kbp](https://rosalind.info/glossary/kbp/)).

**Return:** The Hamming distance dH(s,t)dH(s,t).

## **Sample Dataset**

``` md
GAGCCTACTAACGGGAT
CATCGTAATGACGGCCT
```

## **Sample Output**

``` md
7
```

## Solution

``` bash
str_1="GAGCCTACTAACGGGAT"
str_2="CATCGTAATGACGGCCT"
# str_1=`cat rosalind_hamm.txt | awk '(NR==1){print}'`
# str_2=`cat rosalind_hamm.txt | awk '(NR==2){print}'`

# The length of string 1
str_size=${#str_1}

count=0
for (( i=0; i<=str_size-1; i++ )); do
    #echo ${str_1:i:1} ${str_2:i:1}
    if [ ${str_1:i:1} != ${str_2:i:1} ]; then
        ((count++));
    else
        continue
    fi
done; echo $count
```
